messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide for creating a **GET** request to the *“Get information of device connector versions”* API on Cisco Nexus Dashboard (v6.3.1). The instructions cover both the **Dashboard UI** (API Explorer) and a **manual cURL** example so you can hit the endpoint from any terminal or script. --- ## 1. Locate the API in the Dashboard | Step | What to do | Where to find it | |------|------------|------------------| | 1 | Log in to the Nexus Dashboard. | Top‑right corner → **Admin** → **Developer Tools** | | 2 | Click **API Explorer** (or **Swagger UI** if available). | In the Developer Tools pane | | 3 | Search for the operation “Get information of device connector versions”. | The API list is searchable; the operation name is usually shown in the description. | > **Tip:** If you can’t find the operation, check the **API Documentation** tab. The endpoint is typically documented as `/api/v1/device-connector-versions` (or similar). --- ## 2. Understand the Endpoint | Item | Typical Value | Notes | |------|---------------|-------| | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | Retrieves data only. | | **Path** | `/api/v1/device-connector-versions` | May vary slightly; confirm in the UI. | | **Query Parameters** | `deviceId`, `version`, `page`, `size` (optional) | Only include those you need. | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | Token is required for authentication. | | **Response** | JSON array of connector objects | Each object contains `connectorId`, `name`, `version`, `status`, etc. | --- ## 3. Get an Authentication Token The Nexus Dashboard uses **OAuth 2.0 Bearer tokens** (or sometimes Basic Auth). If you’re using the UI, the token is automatically handled. For a manual request: ```bash # Example: obtain a token via the OAuth token endpoint curl -X POST https:///oauth/token \ -d "grant_type=client_credentials" \ -d "client_id=" \ -d "client_secret=" \ -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" ``` The response will contain `access_token`. Use it in the `Authorization` header. --- ## 4. Build the cURL Request ```bash curl -X GET "https:///api/v1/device-connector-versions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -G \ --data-urlencode "deviceId=12345" \ --data-urlencode "page=1" \ --data-urlencode "size=50" ``` ### Explanation | Part | Purpose | |------|---------| | `-X GET` | Explicitly sets the HTTP method. | | `https:///api/v1/device-connector-versions` | Full endpoint URL. | | `-H "Authorization: Bearer "` | Auth header. | | `-H "Accept: application/json"` | Tell the server we want JSON. | | `-G` | Append data as query string (for GET). | | `--data-urlencode` | Encode query parameters safely. | > **Replace** ``, ``, and any query values with your actual data. --- ## 5. Test the Request in the Dashboard UI 1. In **API Explorer**, select the operation. 2. Fill in any required query parameters. 3. Click **Execute**. 4. The UI will show the raw request, response headers, status code, and pretty‑printed JSON body. 5. Use the **“Copy cURL”** button to copy the exact command (useful for scripts). --- ## 6. Sample Response ```json [ { "connectorId": "c-001", "name": "Cisco Nexus 9000", "version": "9.3.1", "status": "active", "lastUpdated": "2024-06-20T12:34:56Z" }, { "connectorId": "c-002", "name": "Cisco Nexus 7000", "version": "7.2.0", "status": "inactive", "lastUpdated": "2024-05-15T08:22:10Z" } ] ``` --- ## 7. Common Pitfalls & Troubleshooting | Issue | Likely Cause | Fix | |-------|--------------|-----| | **401 Unauthorized** | Token expired or wrong scope | Refresh token or request a new one with correct scopes. | | **404 Not Found** | Wrong endpoint path | Verify the path in the API Explorer. | | **400 Bad Request** | Invalid query parameter | Double‑check parameter names and allowed values. | | **500 Internal Server Error** | Server issue | Retry later or contact support. | --- ## 8. Automating the Call (Python Example) ```python import requests BASE_URL = "https://" TOKEN = "" headers = { "Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}", "Accept": "application/json" } params = { "deviceId": "12345", "page": 1, "size": 50 } resp = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/device-connector-versions", headers=headers, params=params) resp.raise_for_status() data = resp.json() print(data) ``` --- ### Quick Checklist - [ ] Confirm the exact endpoint path in the Dashboard UI. - [ ] Obtain a valid OAuth bearer token. - [ ] Include `Accept: application/json`. - [ ] Add any required query parameters. - [ ] Test in the UI first, then copy the generated cURL or code snippet. That’s it! You now know how to generate and execute a RESTful API request for device connector versions on Cisco Nexus Dashboard v6.3.1. Happy automating!
